camilla: Quick note — I found a CPU-side perf regression in the token pipeline after yesterday's kernel-scheduler tweak. Perfetto trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/1a2b3c4d (private). NSYS summary uploaded to drive: /drive/reports/nsys-token-pipeline-1905.zip. Spike shows long gaps between tokenizer finish and batcher kernel launch, lots of small kernel launches.
jorge: Repro steps? commit sha?
camilla: repro is in infra/harnesses/token_pipeline/run_local.sh. Commit: a3d9b7f. Repro command I used:
```bash
# on m6i-large with 16 vCPU
perf record -F 99 -g -- python3 infra/harnesses/token_pipeline/run_local.py --model llm-small --seq 1024 --batch 8
```
Also ran `python -m pyinstrument` to get Python stack samples.
ash: pushed a small perf script to reproduce kernel-launch latency. Folded stacks from `stackcollapse-perf.pl` show:
```
PyEval_EvalFrameEx;tokenize_bytes;batcher_wait;kernel_launch_overhead  42
PyEval_EvalFrameEx;tokenize_bytes;kernel_init;memcpy           18
syscall;futex_wait;thread_wakeup                            12
```
Looks like GIL hold in tokenizer + subsequent memcpy and kernel launches. The kernel timeline (nsys) shows many ~120-250us kernel launches instead of a few bigger kernels.
perf-bot: CI perf job: https://ci.redwood/teams/eng-runtime/jobs/3912 — flamegraph attached, status: flaky. :eyes:
camilla: From trace + nsys: two issues:
1) kernel selection heuristic flips between `matmul_v1` and `matmul_v2` for the same shapes depending on micro-timing; v2 has better throughput but slightly higher launch latency, so when split into many micro-batches we pay more launch overhead.
2) KV cache eviction path triggers memcpy on hot path when batcher merges shards, introducing 80-140ms spikes.
jorge: Can we get a focused microbench measuring just kernel launch and memcpy latency? I'll run a kernel-only harness and report numbers. Also, which batching window are you using? 5ms?
camilla: Tests used batch_agg_window_ms=5. If I bump to 15ms aggregated tokens, wall latency improves but tail increases slightly. Example quick numbers from local run (seq=1024 batch=8):
- median token latency: 12.6ms -> 10.2ms (after bump)
- p99 token latency: 320ms -> 335ms (worse)
ash: My notes: adding a threshold to prefer matmul_v2 when token_count >= 32 avoids the flip and reduces launch count by ~30%. Also fixed a bug in KV cache where we memcpy even for in-place compatible shards.
camilla: Proposal: add config flag `prefer_v2_threshold_tokens` default 32 + increase batch_agg_window_ms to 10 for CPU tier. I'll open PR with benchmark results and a toggle for canary.
jorge: +1. Add a unit test for kernel-choice deterministic selection given identical inputs and seeds so scheduler changes don't flip it.
ash: I'll add microbench harness to /infra/bench/kernel_launch/ and instrument with CPU rdtsc timing. Quick kernel-only numbers on my laptop: avg launch latency (v1): 180us, (v2): 210us, throughput better for v2 on large matmuls.
perf-bot: note — saved perf map: gs://perf-maps/1905002341-token-pipeline/map.json
camilla: Action items:
- camilla: open PR w/ flag + perf numbers (today)
- ash: add kernel-launch microbench + KV memcpy guard (tomorrow)
- jorge: run kernel-only harness on internal perf box and post results (EOD)
infra-bot: deploy-batcher: canary rollout started for batcher-config-1905 (target=5% traffic) — watch latency dashboards.
ash: one more: add tracing span at tokenizer->batcher handoff so we can correlate GIL hold to kernel launches in perfetto. tiny patch incoming.
camilla: thanks everyone — I'll paste the PR when ready. :thumbsup:
